There Is No Such Thing as a "UN Map With Borders": Guterres

2026-09-13 Suhasini Haidar and Kallol Bhattacherjee (The Hindu) UN, Antonio Guterres, Correct the Map, India, Arunachal Pradesh, Aksai Chin, borders, world map, Equal Earth, UN Geospatial
Read the source article

Quick summary

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres clarified that the UN has never published a map with borders, after India raised "anomalies" about a map used during the "Correct the Map" resolution that omitted Indian and Chinese claim lines in Arunachal Pradesh and Aksai Chin.

Key takeaways

  • UN Secretary-General Guterres stated categorically: "There is no such thing as a 'UN map with borders'" and "it's not for the UN to define" borders
  • The controversial map was created by UN Geospatial during the consultation process for the "Correct the Map" resolution, but Guterres called it "not an official UN map" — "the contribution of an NGO"
  • The map depicted Arunachal Pradesh and Aksai Chin without the Indian and Chinese "claim lines" that previous UN maps had used
  • India had voted in favor of the "Correct the Map" resolution but raised "anomalies" about the map with the UN
  • The map showed the Line of Control in Jammu & Kashmir as a dotted line with an explanatory note, but no similar note for omitted claim lines in Arunachal Pradesh and Aksai Chin
  • MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal clarified India's vote was in support of "equal area representation" principle
  • Guterres emphasized the resolution itself is not a map but a statement that distortions in landmasses "come from power relations of the past"
